task.title: Page finite recurrences sparsely by status
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/997 with bounded exact-ID scan pages filtered by persisted finite-recurrence status.
acceptance_criteria: Inspect at most one positive at-most-1024 recurrence window plus lookahead and return complete exact-status matches in exact-ID order.
Advance continuation from the last inspected recurrence even across all-nonmatching windows.
Canonically validate selected definitions and lookahead while isolating corruption outside bounded work.

attempts.diagnostic: Targeted recurrence-store tests failed because RecurrenceStatusPage and RecurrenceStore::list_by_status_page did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused tests for sparse active and cancelled pages, cursor progress, terminal windows, empty storage, and bounded corruption behavior.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the bounded kernel slice.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented bounded exact-ID selection, complete selected-window replay, persisted-status filtering, and last-inspected continuation.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 997 in crates/vela-kernel/src/scheduler.rs with store tests, ADR-0097, and scheduler documentation; independent review found no blocking issue.

attempts.diagnostic: A rate-limited false green was excluded; after cooldown, CodeRabbit command 68978c3d completed on exact head 69c1a5b with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Preserved the exact verified commit until review capacity returned before enabling squash merge.

outcome.summary: Issue 997 delivered bounded sparse finite-recurrence status paging without adding occurrence or execution authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 998 exact head 69c1a5bc00d1784529d704988859776adc624daf

lessons: A bounded sparse page must define work by inspected inventory, not by the number of matches returned.
Last-inspected recurrence cursors make all-nonmatching pages advance without overlapping scans.
Complete selected-definition replay preserves fail-closed status truth without adding occurrence, lifecycle, clock, or execution authority.
